messages:
support-liz: Filing this thread — customer reports intermittent 403 on /v1/generate. Root req id shared below. Can you paste the exact curl you used and the request-id from the response?

customer-jay: repro steps I ran locally:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTEDabc123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Org-Id: org-777" \n  -H "X-Project-Id: proj-999" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}'
```
Response: 403 with body:
```json
{"error":"forbidden","message":"signature validation failed","request_id":"01f2c3deadbeef"}
```

support-liz: thanks. quick clarifying q: did you generate that token from the org-level service key or a project-scoped key? also if you can paste the exact Authorization header (obfuscate middle) that helps.

customer-jay: token was created from the org admin console (I think org-level). header above is exact except redacted bits — we did add X-Project-Id because our app normally targets proj-999. we recently rotated keys for proj-999 last week. request id again: 01f2c3deadbeef.

eng-jon: I tried to repro using the same headers and token (with obfuscated secret). On our side I initially got 401. Quick server log snippet from auth path:
```
[2026-03-16T18:20:11Z] auth-service ERROR request_id=01f2c3deadbeef path=/v1/generate msg="signature verification failed: public key lookup returned none"
[2026-03-16T18:20:11Z] auth-service DEBUG token_scope=org token_id=tok-0a1b2c
```
This suggests the token is being validated against the project key lookup (not org key).

customer-jay: I uploaded the debug bundle the support collector requested earlier: dbg-7890 (shared link in DM). Also timeline: key rotation for proj-999 happened 2026-03-09.

support-liz: copied dbg-7890, forwarding to infra. Also can you run our quick collector locally if needed?
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/internal/debug/collect \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTEDabc123" \n  -H "X-Org-Id: org-777" \n  -H "X-Project-Id: proj-999" \n  -d '{"request_id":"01f2c3deadbeef"}' | jq -r '.bundle_id'
```
That will emit a bundle id you can paste here.

infra-amy: looked into dbg-7890. Root cause: when both X-Org-Id and X-Project-Id are present our router prefers the project auth flow. The token in question is org-scoped (org-level key) so project flow tries to find a matching project public key and fails (signature lookup returns none) — yields 403/401 depending on parity. During the proj-999 rotation we changed the default mapping to prefer project-level resolution which exposed this mismatch.
Fix options:
- Short term: omit X-Project-Id so org flow validates (what the customer confirmed works).
- Long term: either issue project-scoped token for proj-999 or update the client to map tokens to scopes explicitly.
We can also add a compatibility edge that falls back to org key lookup if project lookup fails, but that requires SRE rollout and audit — planning that now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Compatibility logging patch deployed to auth-service (flags: log-ambiguous-scope=true) — will collect noisy logs for 24h :rocket: 

support-liz: @customer-jay can you confirm if calling without X-Project-Id returns 200 for you? If yes we'll mark the immediate issue as resolved and provide guidance for rotating to a project token.

customer-jay: confirmed — removed X-Project-Id and same curl returns 200 with body and request_id 01f2c3feedface. Looks good. We'll rotate our client to a project-scoped token today. Thanks for the quick triage!

support-liz: great, marking resolved for now. If you see any more 4xx/5xx after rotating to a project token ping this thread and attach the new request_id.
